principle: QUALITY FIRST, TOKENS SECOND (the owner, 2026-10-28, every class and chapter): no visual compromise, the best result, and every necessary check. Nothing that proves a tool is right is skipped, thinned or shortened to save tokens or time: the maths review of the final English, the language pass (tr-coverage), the FULL visual review (every frame of the review pack in English, Hindi and Gujarati), the play test where a tool is new or risky (real input), the image pass, and the final full check on 0 FAIL, then the upload audit for the chapter. Tokens are saved only by how the work is done: one chapter per session and contexts under 100k, reviewers working from the review pack, digests and check rows instead of whole sources, packs built once per round and re-looks on changed frames only, quick and cached checks before ONE full check, batched maths, language, image and audit work, reports of at most 40 lines, image reuse, Sonnet (no cap) for every look and Opus (5 at once) where it shortens the critical path. Adaptive mode means this, never a thinner review.

defaults.agentCaps: the owner, 2026-10-28, every class and chapter: at most 5 Opus agents RUNNING at once (a builder or reviewer launched on Opus counts), no cap on Sonnet or Haiku agents (null = none), as many as the chapter needs; this overrides the builders 4 / reviewers 2 / Opus 4 of before and any older cap written in a chapter's NOTES.md; builders and play testers each drive a headless Chrome and more than 6 at once gave false timeouts, so the gate notes it (a note, not a limit)

sprint.note: While `node orch.mjs sprint` runs for ONE tool (runbook 'Sprint mode', the owner 2026-10-28): up to 5 Opus agents at once (simple or complex tool) and no cap on Sonnet agents; since 2026-10-28 these are also the standing figures, the owner's word, so a sprint lifts no cap (the gate takes the higher of the standing figure and the sprint's own). No review is dropped; the extra agents run the looks in parallel. Everything else in `defaults` still applies, and it ends with `sprint stop`.

tiers.tier2: full check only for changed tools
tiers.tier3: real-input play test for new or risky interactions
tiers.tier4: review pack only for visual changes
